newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Mexican miller sees wheat output at 4 mln Tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Mexican miller sees wheat output at 4 mln Tonnes.

text.p: Mexican wheat output may rise to about four million tonnes in 1997 from 3.8 million tonnes this year, a top milling official said Tuesday.

"We may possibly manage four million tonnes of wheat," Luis Galindo Martin, president of Mexico's Federal District Flour Milling Chamber, told Reuters in an interview at the assembly of Latin American Millers (ALIM) in Paraguay's capital.
Mexican farmers harvested about 3.8 million tonnes of wheat this year, including 600,000 tonnes of amber durum wheat, which is not suitable for bread making.
Galindo said he expected durum acreage to fall in sowing that starts in November: "We expect a greater volume of bread wheat to be sown, taking away area from amber durum."

Higher local output should reduce Mexican wheat imports, which presently come exclusively from North American Free Trade Association partners the United States and Canada. While a 10.5-percent import tariff is levied on Canadian and U.S. wheat, millers are not permitted to import from outside NAFTA without a government permit.

"We are captive clients for the United States and Canada," said Galindo, who added that millers were lobbying the government to allow them to import freely from other countries, but that they were not making much progress.
He said Mexico will import about 1.5 million tonnes of wheat this year, with about 70 percent coming from the United States.
Mexico's milling industry is operating only 70 percent of its installed capacity and has taken a battering from the country's economic crisis.

Another problem is competition with traditional maize tortillas, which are subsidized and so cheaper than bread. Mexicans eat eight million tonnes of maize a year. Bread has recently lost its subsidy.
Galindo said he expected to see only a small recovery in bread consumption in 1997.
